prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has knee injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1101; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're okay to continue?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Can you describe where you were driving when the collision happened?

A: I was heading down a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right lane. Traffic had slowed up ahead because of a light that had turned red.

Q: What happened next?

A: I came to a stop behind a car at the light. About a few seconds later, I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No, I didn't. I was looking at the light and the car in front of me. I only noticed it when I heard the brakes squeal and then the impact.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?

A: I did, but my left knee gave out when I stepped down. It struck the door frame and I had to hold onto the car to stay upright.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment for your knee?

A: Yes. I was taken to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and said there was swelling and some ligament soreness. I've been told to keep weight off it for a while and to follow up with an orthopedic doctor.

Q: Is there anything else about the accident you'd like to add?

A: Only that my car has damage to the rear bumper and trunk, and I'm still having trouble walking up stairs. I'll send over the clinic paperwork when I get home.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you once we've reviewed everything.

A: Thanks, I appreciate it.
